item.title: The Transverse Finiteness Conjecture for pseudo-Anosov flows via universal circles
item.description: arXiv:2611.33320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove Mosher's Transverse Finiteness Conjecture, posed in 1996. This states that every taut, finite depth foliation $\mathcal F$ of an atoroidal 3-manifold is almost transverse to at most finitely many pseudo-Anosov flows, up to orbit equivalence. Our strategy is to organize the flows that are almost transverse to $\mathcal F$ using their associated universal circles. This technique also establishes the following rigidity result: if a finite depth foliation $\mathcal F$ is almost transverse to a pseudo-Anosov flow $\varphi$ without perfect fits, then $\varphi$ is the unique pseudo-Anosov flow that is almost transverse to $\mathcal F$, up to orbit equivalence. In fact, in this setting, $\mathcal F$ has only one minimal universal circle.
item.dc:creator: Michael P. Landry, Samuel J. Taylor

item.title: Size-preserving Cromwell equivalence for unknotted grid diagrams
item.description: arXiv:2611.33834v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate that every grid diagram representing the unknot is equivalent, via Cromwell moves which preserve the grid number, to a grid diagram with no crossings, sharpening a monotonic-simplification result of Dynnikov. Moreover, we enumerate the equivalence classes of grid diagrams for the unknot, considered up to size-preserving Cromwell moves. As an application, we generate all grid diagrams for the unknot through grid number $8$ and identify the first examples of weakly Cromwell hard grid diagrams for the unknot.
item.dc:creator: Austin Christian, James Rea, Matthew Stark

item.title: Norm groups of orders and the algebraic unknotting number
item.description: arXiv:2611.34200v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We use number-theoretic tools to find an explicit and effective obstruction for a knot to have algebraic unknotting number equal to $1$. As an example, we show that the connected sum of $T(2,5)$ (the cinquefoil) and $-T(2,3)$ (the negative trefoil) has algebraic unknotting number $1$, even though $T(2,5)$ has algebraic unknotting number $2$.
item.dc:creator: Maciej Borodzik, Wojciech Politarczyk

item.title: A Short Proof of the Goldman--Parker Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.34289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Goldman and Parker conjectured that the three order-two complex side reflections of an ideal triangle with Cartan angular invariant $A$ define a discrete and faithful representation of $\mathbb Z/2 \ast \mathbb Z/2 \ast \mathbb Z/2$ in $PU(2,1)$ whenever $\tan^2 A\le 125/3$. Schwartz first proved the conjecture using rigorous computer-assisted estimates and later gave an analytic proof based on three loxodromic $\mathbb R$-spheres. We give a substantially shorter proof of this conjecture using a simpler geometric construction. For parameters just below the critical value, we use the Cygan bisector of the two fixed points of the triple product of the reflections. This wall and one of its cusp translates bound a strip from which we construct a trapping region. At the critical value $\tan^2 A=125/3$, the two fixed points merge, and the same construction applies to the limiting wall.
item.dc:creator: Krishnendu Gongopadhyay, Anna Pratoussevitch

item.title: A fake quadric that is not a bidisk quotient
item.description: arXiv:2611.33669v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fake quadrics are minimal complex surfaces of general type with $b_1=0$ and $e=4$. The paper gives a construction of a fake quadric $S$ that is a $32$-fold branched cover of $\mathbf{CP}^1\times\mathbf{CP}^1$ along nine curves. This configuration is given by four horizontal lines, four vertical lines and the diagonal. We show that $S$ is not aspherical. As a corollary the universal cover of $S$ is not the bidisk $\mathbf{H}\times\mathbf{H}$.
item.dc:creator: Zolt\'an Szab\'o

item.title: Fixed points for actions of automorphism groups of free products on ${\rm CAT(0)}$ spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.33876v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study fixed-point properties of automorphism groups of free products acting on complete ${\rm CAT(0)}$ spaces. Under the assumption of certain fixed-point properties of the free factors, we obtain lower bounds on the smallest dimension in which automorphism groups can act on a complete ${\rm CAT(0)}$ space without a global fixed point.
item.dc:creator: Qian Chen, Qiang Zhang, Dongxiao Zhao

item.title: Colored Jones polynomial of figure eight knot and non-perturbative topological recursion
item.description: arXiv:2611.34110v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The asymptotic expansion of the colored Jones polynomial of the figure eight knot is proved to be connected with non-perturbative topological recursion on the underlying elliptic spectral curve, following the proposal of Borot and Eynard.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Hock, Sergey Shadrin

item.title: Mixed tori in contact surgery diagrams
item.description: arXiv:2510.19580v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a diagrammatic framework for applying the symplectic JSJ decomposition to exact/weak symplectic fillings of 3-dimensional contact manifolds. Namely, we apply the symplectic JSJ decomposition to a contact surgery diagram for some $(Y,\zeta)$, producing a finite collection of contact manifolds, also described diagrammatically, whose exact/weak symplectic fillings determine those of $(Y,\zeta)$. We apply this technique to recover known symplectic filling classifications for certain lens spaces and torus bundles, and also to provide an algorithm for classifying the exact/weak symplectic fillings of a large class of plumbed 3-manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Austin Christian, Tanushree Shah

item.title: On the crossing number of knots and links on surfaces in 3-manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2606.18776v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a lower bound of the minimum crossing number of knots and links projected on a 2-sided surface in a 3-manifold using the rank of fundamental groups which means that the crossing number can take arbitrary large values. On the contrary, we show that for a branched surface, the minimum crossing number is always zero. As an application, we give an upper bound of the three-page index by the crossing number.
item.dc:creator: Tetsuya Ito

item.title: An elementary proof that linking problems are hard
item.description: arXiv:2509.13120v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a new, elementary proof of what we believe is the simplest known example of a "natural" problem in computational 3-dimensional topology that is NP-hard---namely, the Trivial Sublink Problem: given a diagram $L$ of a link in $S^3$ and a positive integer $k$, decide if $L$ contains a $k$ component sublink that is trivial. This problem was previously shown to be NP-hard in independent works of Koenig-Tsvietkova and de Mesmay-Rieck-Sedgwick-Tancer, both of which used reductions from 3SAT. The reduction we describe instead starts with the Independent Set Problem, and allows us to avoid the use of Brunnian links such as the Borromean rings. On the technical level, this entails a new conceptual insight: the Trivial Sublink Problem is hard entirely due to mod 2 pairwise linking, with no need for integral or higher order linking. On the pedagogical level, the reduction we describe is entirely elementary, and thus suitable for introducing undergraduates and non-experts to complexity-theoretic low-dimensional topology. To drive this point home, in this work we assume no familiarity with low-dimensional topology, and---other than Reidemeister's Theorem and Karp's result that the Clique Problem is NP-hard---we provide more-or-less complete definitions and proofs. We have also constructed a web app that accompanies this work and allows a user to visualize the new reduction interactively.
item.dc:creator: Shannon Cheng, Anna Chlopecki, Saarah Nazar, Eric Samperton

item.title: A new class of affine $K(\pi,1)$ arrangements
item.description: arXiv:2512.00318v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that a certain class of affine hyperplane arrangements are $K(\pi,1)$ by endowing their Falk complexes with an injective metric. This gives new examples of infinite $K(\pi,1)$ arrangements in dimension $n>2$.
item.dc:creator: Katherine Goldman, Jingyin Huang

item.title: $G_2'$-Slodowy Slices II: Anosov Representations
item.description: arXiv:2611.14503v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We find many exotic connected components of Anosov representations of surface groups in the split real group $G_2'$ that are neither $\iota$-Fuchsian deformations nor higher rank Teichm\"uller spaces. These representations are found through the non-abelian Hodge correspondence via $G_2'$-Higgs bundles that we call $\alpha$-bundles and $\beta$-bundles, which are particular cyclic Higgs bundles in the Slodowy slices of the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-triples associated to the simple roots $\alpha$ and $\beta$ of $\mathfrak{g}_2^{\mathbb{C}}$. We first prove that (most) $\beta$-bundles that are also Hodge bundles are $P_{\beta}$-Anosov and $\alpha$-bundles are $P_{\alpha}$-Anosov. The strategy employed is new, geometric, and general. For $\sigma \in \{\alpha, \beta\}$, we then show the locally homogeneous $(G_2', G_2'/P_{\sigma})$-manifold $\mathscr{M}_{\sigma}(\rho)$ recently described in arXiv:2510.12757, for the representation $\rho:\pi_1S\rightarrow \mathsf{G}_2'$ associated to a $\sigma$-bundle, coincides up to finite cover with the corresponding geometric structure for $\rho$ defined via domains of discontinuity by Guichard-Wienhard and Kapovich-Leeb-Porti. Consequently, we find that $\pi_1({\mathscr{M}}_{\sigma}(\rho))$ is an invariant for the connected component of $\rho$ in the space of $P_{\sigma}$-Anosov representations. After verifying the folklore result that the $G_2'$-character variety has exactly three connected components, we conclude lower bounds for the number of connected components of $P_{\sigma}$-Anosov representations in the two non-Hitchin components, most of which are exotic. These are the first higher rank examples of connected components of a character variety containing multiple (in fact, arbitrarily many) exotic components of Anosov representations.
item.dc:creator: Colin Davalo, Parker Evans
